inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,203 splitlines of the normalized survey. The source builds a working notion of harmonic and geometric families of automorphic L-functions, derives vertical local measures and coarse Sato–Tate indicators, separates Sato–Tate equidistribution from the deeper low-zero universality conjecture, tests the framework on arithmetic, spectral, twisting, product, and monodromy examples, and records sharp limitations from thin, Diophantine, and measure-zero parameter sets. Both appendices supply material bridges: Weil–Deligne/local Langlands and geometric automorphy in Appendix A, and a conditional motivic sign argument excluding central criticality for regular C-algebraic orthogonal representations in Appendix B. Formula extraction is imperfect in places but the selected claims remain recoverable from checked prose and displayed relations.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the aim of predicting family symmetry classes from basic invariants.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Motivation and invariants of individual representations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates deformation in families and defines conductor, duality type, root number, and individual Sato–Tate measure.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Harmonic and geometric family formation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the two construction routes and admissible operations, gauges, and boundaries.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Counting, vertical limits, and Conjecture 1
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Imposes finiteness and infinitude and formulates local equidistribution and the family Sato–Tate measure.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Indicators, rank, and root number
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compresses family type into trace moments and separates persistent central zeros from root-number splitting.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Low-lying zeros and Conjecture 2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines conductor scaling and maps homogeneous types to random-matrix universality classes while stating evidential limits.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1. Degree-one and quadratic-character families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Provides an explicit model family and a function-field transfer mechanism for density identities.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2. Number fields and Artin L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs families by specialization and invariant-theoretic parametrization and reads symmetry from finite Galois images.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3. Families of elliptic curves
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares height and conductor ordering and separates monodromy type, geometric rank, and average root number.

sections_inspected.label: 2.4. Dwork families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses an invariant cohomology summand and parity-dependent monodromy to predict symmetry.

sections_inspected.label: 2.5. Harmonic families and Plancherel equidistribution
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the trace-formula route from Weyl law to quantitative local equidistribution and its Maass-form bottleneck.

sections_inspected.label: 2.6. Invariants of harmonic families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies Sato–Tate groups and indicators from the dual-group representation and isolates analytic-continuation dependencies.

sections_inspected.label: 2.7. Classical modular forms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Instantiates Plancherel, root-number splitting, support limits, and low-zero densities for PGL(2).

sections_inspected.label: 2.8. GL(1) twists
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Computes family measures as pushforwards under scalar multiplication and contrasts thin quadratic twists with all-character twists.

sections_inspected.label: 2.9. Rankin–Selberg products
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Tracks indicators through tensor products and exposes central-value weighting as a symmetry confound.

sections_inspected.label: 2.10. Universal families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates universal local measures to conductor strata of Plancherel measure and distinguishes failure of a vertical limit from low-zero universality.

sections_inspected.label: 2.11. Deligne–Katz equidistribution
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reduces geometric-family averages to finite fields and derives the limiting measure from geometric monodromy.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1. Limitations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows why unrestricted Diophantine bases and intersections can destroy countability asymptotics and statistics.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2. Fields of rationality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Studies families cut out by bounded rationality fields and their conjectural relation to geometric families.

sections_inspected.label: 3.3. Measure-zero local conditions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies a trace-formula isolation failure for spectrally null constraints.

sections_inspected.label: 3.4. Universal H-types
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contrasts inaccessible universal type classes with constructible geometric subfamilies and class-field cases.

sections_inspected.label: 3.5. Hybrid and restricted families
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Combines number-field and harmonic variation and notes factor removal, thin restrictions, and mixed types.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix A. Hasse–Weil L-functions
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines local/global Galois L-data and states automorphy and Galois–automorphic correspondence conjectures with normalization caveats.

sections_inspected.label: Appendix B. Non-criticality
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Gives a conditional motivic sign argument that regular algebraic orthogonal L-functions lack a critical central value.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-depth-bearing scholarly apparatus.

accepted_units.title: Why individual L-functions are deformed inside families
accepted_units.why_material: Connects family averaging to density theorems, subconvexity, and function-field deformation, and frames low-zero statistics as a family-level phenomenon distinct from high-zero GUE behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the motivating contrast between individual and family questions and the announced harmonic, geometric, and geometry-of-numbers tools.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: conceptual prose; displayed notation is not needed.

accepted_units.title: Analytic conductor, functional equation, and duality type
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the ordering/complexity variable and the orthogonal-versus-symplectic distinction via poles of symmetric- and exterior-square factors, which later drive family symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the isobaric reduction and root-number normalization needed to interpret the classification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: factorization and pole placement are essential but legible in the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Individual Sato–Tate measures and non-unique group realizations
accepted_units.why_material: Moves from local components to a limiting measure and observes that different compact-group embeddings can yield the same measure, making the measure rather than a uniquely named group the stable invariant.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the trace-moment constraints and the definition of the admissible measure set.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: matrix eigenvalue and trace-integral notation supports the prose; formulas are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Harmonic families from trace-formula-isolable spectral sets
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a reusable spectral construction: isolate a large automorphic set on H, then transfer it through an L-group representation to GL(n).
accepted_units.context_note: Read with the opening definition of a parametric family at lines 137–140.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the dual-group map and pushforward notation are material.

accepted_units.title: Geometric families from specialized cohomology
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the geometric route from a smooth proper family over an affine base to specialized étale-cohomology L-functions and, conditionally, automorphic representations.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the cone restriction, constant cohomology dimension, and unitary determinant twist.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: cohomological degree and determinant twist are formula-dependent, though the surrounding prose resolves their roles.

accepted_units.title: Gauge ordering, family operations, and the Diophantine boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why discriminant gauges can stand in for conductor, how unions/products preserve parametrization, and why intersections can introduce uncontrolled Diophantine sets.
accepted_units.context_note: Also distinguishes natural arithmetic collections from the narrower class currently analyzable by the framework.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose with simple product-map notation.

accepted_units.title: Finiteness, infinitude, and vertical coefficient limits
accepted_units.why_material: Specifies the nondegeneracy conditions that make asymptotic family statistics meaningful and expresses averaged Dirichlet coefficients through local-density main terms with power-saving error.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes exclusions for non-finite-to-one and isotrivial maps and the role of shells versus balls.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (3)–(5) encode the core averaging interface; text extraction is sufficient but should be checked against the PDF for exact symbols.

accepted_units.title: Family Sato–Tate equidistribution as a vertical local measure
accepted_units.why_material: Conjecture 1 makes the family a probability distribution on local representations, permits a finite convex product decomposition, and defines the horizontal Sato–Tate limit over primes.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the statistically-negligible interpretation of nonunitary local exceptions and the weight-monodromy caveat.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the product space, prime average, and convex-measure conditions are integral to the claim.

accepted_units.title: Three trace indicators recover cuspidal, self-dual, and sign type
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how three low-order trace moments classify generic cuspidality, self-duality, and orthogonal/symplectic type and uniquely recover their mixture proportions even when group decomposition is nonunique.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the zero first moment and Frobenius–Schur interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (7)–(10) and their inequalities carry the compression mechanism.

accepted_units.title: From product measures to homogeneous subfamilies, but not canonical groups
accepted_units.why_material: Suggests a density-weighted decomposition into irreducible homogeneous pieces while explaining why a general family Sato–Tate group is neither uniquely determined nor tractable for thin families.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly heuristic beyond Conjecture 1, not a proved decomposition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: conceptual measure/group distinction.

accepted_units.title: Family rank measures persistent central zeros through a secondary local term
accepted_units.why_material: Relates generic rational cycles to a next-order prime average and explains why universal fluctuations should be studied only after removing family-persistent central zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the elliptic-surface/Tate-conjecture interpretation and the rank-zero simplification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (11) and its square-root scaling are essential; verify typography if reused formally.

accepted_units.title: Root-number splitting requires Möbius-type cancellation
accepted_units.why_material: Separates local Sato–Tate type from the functional-equation sign and identifies polynomial Möbius cancellation as the extra arithmetic input needed to split a symplectic family by root number.
accepted_units.context_note: The four homogeneous classes are obtained only after the sign split.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the schematic Möbius sum and decomposition are central but prose recovers the mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Conductor-scaled low zeros and the universality dictionary
accepted_units.why_material: Defines universal zero scaling by analytic conductor and maps unitary, orthogonal, and sign-refined symplectic families to the four limiting compact-group laws and r-level densities.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes removal of the forced central zero and the weighted-mixture rule for nonhomogeneous families.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: scaling equation (14), two classification tables, and density labels must remain attached to the prose.

accepted_units.title: Local equidistribution is shallower than low-zero universality
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes the comparatively accessible local Sato–Tate theorem from universality, which needs analytic continuation and deeper cancellation, and uses function-field cohomology to explain the apparent duality reversal of symmetry.
accepted_units.context_note: Also records numerical evidence and the odd-rank orthogonal consequence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: conceptual prose with a cohomological pairing.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic characters as a fully explicit orthogonal family
accepted_units.why_material: Realizes the same family both spectrally and geometrically and computes its local measure, rank, indicators, and predicted symplectic low-zero law.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the base example used later for twisting constructions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the family equation and invariant values are material.

accepted_units.title: Function-field averaging certifies number-field density identities
accepted_units.why_material: Defines r-level density for quadratic characters and explains how matching function-field calculations plus uniformity in q force difficult combinatorial identities in the number-field limit.
accepted_units.context_note: Separates the conjectural full density statement from support-restricted theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equations (16)–(18), kernels, and support regions are extraction-sensitive; the prose safely supports the transfer mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Hilbert specialization and Chebotarev determine Artin-family type
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a family from generic polynomial specializations and shows how finite-field counting yields vertical local limits converging to the Haar measure of the fixed Galois image.
accepted_units.context_note: Conductor ordering requires discriminant control and enough parameters relative to degree.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the representation map and discriminant ordering matter; narrative remains readable.

accepted_units.title: Prehomogeneous parametrizations turn field counting into family statistics
accepted_units.why_material: Uses orbit parametrizations and geometry of numbers to count cubic through quintic fields by discriminant, then reads symplectic low-zero symmetry from orthogonal standard representations of symmetric groups.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the cuspform factor obtained after removing the zeta factor and the thin cusp-control issue near discriminant zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: invariant-theoretic actions and zeta-factor identities are material.

accepted_units.title: Elliptic-family invariants depend on the ordering interface
accepted_units.why_material: Shows geometric monodromy gives a pure symplectic family, while moving from height to conductor introduces square-free-sieve and average-conductor questions; family rank is independently geometric.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes universal and one-parameter families and the Tate-conjecture interpretation of rank.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: discriminant, conductor-height ratio, and rank estimates are formula-dependent but prose identifies the conclusions.

accepted_units.title: Geometric rank and root-number bias vary independently
accepted_units.why_material: Exhibits constant negative root number at different family ranks and relates average signs to the nodal factor of the discriminant and Möbius cancellation, preventing conflation of two central-zero mechanisms.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes unconditional low-degree cancellation examples and consequences for average analytic rank.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: explicit curve equations are examples; the independence claim is textual.

accepted_units.title: Dwork invariant cohomology converts parity of monodromy into symmetry
accepted_units.why_material: Extracts an H0-invariant middle-cohomology summand, controls ramification by the discriminant, and uses symplectic versus orthogonal monodromy according to parity to predict low-zero classes.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is conditional on the stated automorphy conjectures, while monodromy and Deligne–Katz equidistribution supply the local type.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the hypersurface equation, group quotient, cohomology superscripts, and parity must be scan-checked before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Quantitative Plancherel equidistribution from the trace formula
accepted_units.why_material: Explains the harmonic route: Weyl-law counting, a uniform trace-formula estimate for local test functions, and pushforward of unramified Plancherel measure to obtain the family local distributions.
accepted_units.context_note: The hard uniformity lies in bounding nonidentity orbital integrals across unbounded conjugacy classes.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: equation (21) carries the quantitative error and support interface.

accepted_units.title: Eisenstein and residual spectra obstruct higher-rank Maass equidistribution
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the known Weyl law from the stronger quantitative local equidistribution and identifies continuous/residual spectrum control as the bottleneck.
accepted_units.context_note: This qualifies extension of the discrete-series harmonic method to spherical archimedean factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose.

accepted_units.title: Dual-group representation determines harmonic-family invariants
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies the family Sato–Tate group with the image of the dual group, equates irreducibility and self-duality properties with the three indicators, proves rank zero from Plancherel decay, and leaves root-number splitting as the subtle residue.
accepted_units.context_note: For nonsplit groups the prime average is Frobenian rather than a literal pointwise limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: indicator values and the O(p^-1) estimate are essential.

accepted_units.title: Partial L-functions make universality robust to ramified-factor uncertainty
accepted_units.why_material: Argues that Ramanujan bounds prevent ramified local poles from cancelling relevant zeros, so low-zero universality can be formulated using partial L-functions and support is controlled by the quality of equidistribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Also notes invariance under sufficiently large finite-place-constrained spectral subsets.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: half-plane inequalities matter but are legible.

accepted_units.title: Classical modular forms separate sign equidistribution from detectable support
accepted_units.why_material: Computes the SU(2) Sato–Tate law and symplectic family type, splits root signs through ramified Plancherel mass, and shows why Fourier support beyond one is needed to distinguish three orthogonal/symplectic density laws.
accepted_units.context_note: The one-level statement removes the forced zero in the negative-sign family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: explicit measure, root-number formula, density equation (22), and support intervals are important.

accepted_units.title: Quadratic twisting pushes forward the individual Sato–Tate measure
accepted_units.why_material: Expresses the thin twist-family measure as the average of an individual measure and its negative, revealing why local family equidistribution can remain as hard as the individual Sato–Tate conjecture while coarse indicators are easier.
accepted_units.context_note: The universality type can be recovered from pole data even if the full individual measure is unknown.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: pushforward equation (23) and trace parity are the operative transformation.

accepted_units.title: Averaging over all characters forces unitary universality
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing quadratic scalars by the full unit circle annihilates the self-duality indicators, making the family unitary independently of the fixed cuspform and relating this to an infinite-center Sato–Tate group.
accepted_units.context_note: Contrasts a rich twisting family with the thin family in the preceding unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: convolution/pushforward notation and indicator values are material.

accepted_units.title: Frobenius–Schur signs multiply under Rankin–Selberg products
accepted_units.why_material: Shows a self-dual product family can have fixed even functional equation without symmetry being reducible to root signs, and proposes multiplicativity of the third indicator under family tensor product.
accepted_units.context_note: The degree-six example supplies a restricted-support confirmation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: tensor embedding and indicator multiplication are central.

accepted_units.title: Adjoint and spin families expose the danger of natural weights
accepted_units.why_material: Derives orthogonal adjoint and symplectic spin types from invariant bilinear forms, then shows central-L-value weights introduced by a trace formula can distort observed symmetry and must be removed for interpretation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes negligible noncuspidal Saito–Kurokawa lifts as evidence for essential cuspidality.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: representation embeddings and indicator values matter; qualitative weighting warning is textual.

accepted_units.title: Vertical Sato–Tate limits can fail along arithmetic exhaustions while universality survives
accepted_units.why_material: Models universal local measures by conductor strata of Plancherel measure but records level sequences for which coefficient-limit equidistribution fails even though low-zero universality is still expected or proved.
accepted_units.context_note: This directly separates Conjecture 1 as formulated from the deeper robustness of Conjecture 2.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the explicit GL(1) mixture illustrates the mechanism but exact coefficients should be scan-checked.

accepted_units.title: Geometric averages localize to residue classes away from the discriminant
accepted_units.why_material: Shows local factors depend only on parameters modulo p, making the family measure atomic; Lang–Weil makes ramification negligible and lattice equidistribution reduces the vertical average to a finite-field problem.
accepted_units.context_note: The affine-base and cone hypotheses are functional inputs, not presentation conveniences.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: local determinant formula and equations (24)–(25) carry exact measure normalization.

accepted_units.title: Deligne–Katz turns geometric monodromy into the family Sato–Tate law
accepted_units.why_material: Packages fiber cohomology as a lisse sheaf, separates arithmetic and geometric monodromy, normalizes Frobenius by purity, and obtains Haar equidistribution on a maximal compact group independent of large p.
accepted_units.context_note: The resulting canonical proof-produced group is geometric monodromy, despite abstract nonuniqueness from the measure alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: fundamental-group representations, pushforwards, and weak convergence in equation (26) are essential.

accepted_units.title: Scheme Sato–Tate tolerates bases that family statistics do not
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts prime-power averaging for a fixed scheme with parameter-family averaging, warning that mild geometric base hypotheses for one do not guarantee meaningful arithmetic statistics for the other.
accepted_units.context_note: Prepares the explicit counterexamples of Section 3.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose.

accepted_units.title: Diophantine parameter sets can encode arbitrary recursive behavior
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why general bases and intersections cease to be analyzable and constructs a quadratic-character image whose real subfamily realizes an arbitrary recursive subset, defeating universal asymptotics.
accepted_units.context_note: The problem is not that the ambient parametric family is invalid, but that an image/intersection discards the controlled parameter geometry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: the polynomial encoding and square-free-part character map support the counterexample.

accepted_units.title: Field-of-rationality cuts may be finite or secretly geometric
accepted_units.why_material: Defines bounded-rationality subfamilies, asks whether the two conjectures hold when they are infinite, and develops evidence and obstructions for realizing them through motives or geometric moduli.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the weight-two elliptic-curve identification, higher-weight Calabi–Yau proposal, and the warning that infinitude lacks a general criterion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: field-degree predicates and cohomological degrees matter but prose is clear.

accepted_units.title: Measure-zero local constraints defeat trace-formula isolation
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies families with fixed cohomological or algebraic archimedean type as natural but outside positive-Plancherel-volume methods, making even their growth hard before local or zero statistics can be tested.
accepted_units.context_note: The same issue applies at finite places.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: conceptual spectral conditions.

accepted_units.title: Universal H-type classes versus constructible geometric subfamilies
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the inaccessible class of all cuspforms with a prescribed hypothetical Sato–Tate group against Hilbert-specialized geometric subfamilies and class-field cases where type and symmetry are computable.
accepted_units.context_note: Makes explicit that defining the individual group and counting the class are separate obstacles.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: group-type prose; finite cyclic and dihedral examples anchor it.

accepted_units.title: Hybrid field/spectral variation and arithmetic restrictions
accepted_units.why_material: Combines varying number fields with functorial lift and automorphic induction, permits removal of common factors, and records how conductor shells, prime conductors, and mixed Galois types complicate otherwise natural families.
accepted_units.context_note: These are extensions beyond the initial family formations, not a claim that all restrictions preserve the conjectures.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium: induced L-group representation and factorization are material.

accepted_units.title: Weil–Deligne data and local Langlands preserve L-factors and conductors
accepted_units.why_material: Provides the local bridge used throughout geometric families: a Weil–Deligne representation with monodromy maps bijectively to an irreducible smooth GL(n) representation while preserving local analytic invariants.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes explicit conductor and inertia-fixed local-factor definitions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: subscripts, inertia invariants, nilpotent kernels, and determinant formulas are extraction-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Geometric Galois representations are conjecturally exactly algebraic automorphic data
accepted_units.why_material: Builds global L-functions from local Weil–Deligne realizations, defines coming from geometry, states geometric automorphy, and reformulates it as a unique L-algebraic automorphic/algebraic l-adic correspondence with local-global compatibility.
accepted_units.context_note: Clearly separates conjectural bijection and compatibility from listed known cases such as elliptic modularity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: twists, cohomological subquotients, and normalization labels must remain exact.

accepted_units.title: The unitary normalization is unconditional only at good reduction
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why twisting degree-d cohomology by |det|^(d/2) places good-reduction Satake parameters on the unit circle, while bad-reduction unitarity remains conditional on weight-monodromy.
accepted_units.context_note: This repairs a hidden assumption in the geometric-family definition.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: sign and exponent of the determinant twist are essential.

accepted_units.title: Regular algebraic orthogonal representations have noncritical center
accepted_units.why_material: Under the stated motivic and correspondence conjectures, translates central criticality into even motive rank and then uses the Galois sign theorem to force symplectic type, contradicting orthogonality; examples distinguish Dirichlet and elliptic cases.
accepted_units.context_note: The proposition statement is unconditional in meaning, but the supplied proof explicitly assumes the motivic correspondence and sign inputs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: weight shifts, pairings, parity, and Hodge indices are formula-sensitive; one duplicated-looking Hodge index at line 1939 should be scan-verified before exact quotation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From local distributions to low-zero symmetry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A family-level pipeline runs from vertical local measures through trace-moment type and an independent root-sign split to conductor-scaled low-zero universality.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The final arrow is Conjecture 2 and needs analytic continuation and cancellation not supplied by Conjecture 1.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Parallel spectral and geometric proofs of Sato–Tate type
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Trace-formula Plancherel equidistribution and finite-field monodromy equidistribution are parallel routes that push a natural local measure through a representation into the same family Sato–Tate interface.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Their hypotheses, error mechanisms, and canonical proof-produced groups differ and should not be identified beyond that interface.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Thinness makes group naming as hard as an individual problem
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Rich scalar averaging can wash out individual structure and force unitary type, whereas thin twisting retains the individual Sato–Tate difficulty and arithmetic exhaustions may even destroy vertical limits.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Low-zero universality can remain robust despite failure or inaccessibility of the full local measure.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Rank and root sign are orthogonal sources of central zeros
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Persistent geometric rank is encoded in a secondary local average, while forced parity zeros come from independently distributed root numbers governed by ramified local data and Möbius-like cancellation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The examples establish independence within the surveyed families, not a universal probabilistic independence theorem.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Operations transform symmetry through representation theory
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Products and twists act on Sato–Tate measures by tensor or scalar pushforward, so low-order indicators can often be propagated without knowing the full measure.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Intersections and thin restrictions need not preserve family statistics, and root-number data requires separate treatment.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Cohomological duality explains symmetry reversal
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Alternating versus symmetric pairings in fiber cohomology or motivic realizations convert orthogonal/symplectic representation type into the opposite-looking compact-group law for low zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The appendix sign argument is conditional and the universality identification remains conjectural outside proved support ranges.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Conditioning can destroy a lawful family
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A controlled ambient parametrization does not guarantee controlled statistics after Diophantine intersection, measure-zero local conditioning, sparse exhaustion, or arithmetic restriction.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some named restrictions may still work by additional methods; the source gives obstructions to a general closure principle.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The geometry-to-automorphy bridge has a normalization fault line
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Weil–Deligne local data and conjectural global automorphy transport geometric cohomology into automorphic families, with a degree-dependent twist enforcing unitary normalization.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: At bad reduction, unitarity and full local-global compatibility retain explicit conjectural dependencies.
